dek: Nas, Slick Rick and Hip-Hop legends become X-Men in a new Marvel comic series.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Nas and Slick Rick joined comic artist *Sanford Greene* at New York Comic Con to unveil their new Marvel superhero forms.

slides.label: The Comic
slides.text: It's part of *Legend Has It*, a new Marvel and Mass Appeal comic series that launched at NYCC in October 2025.

slides.label: Who's In It
slides.text: The series also turns Ghostface Killah, Raekwon, Mobb Deep, Big L and De La Soul into superheroes.

slides.label: The Artist
slides.text: Artist *Sanford Greene* (Bitter Root, Power Man and Iron Fist) designed every character himself.

slides.label: The Design
slides.text: He built Slick Rick's look around his jewelry and *regal* presence, and Nas's around his vivid storytelling.

slides.label: Full Circle
slides.text: Nas called sharing the stage with one of his own heroes, Slick Rick, *'everything'* to him.

slides.label: The Message
slides.text: Slick Rick called Hip-Hop *'the future of civilization'*, one that needs protecting from forces trying to stop its growth.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: Hip-Hop built its own legends from scratch, now it's building its own superhero universe, on its own terms.

caption_instagram:
Nas and Slick Rick just became Marvel superheroes, and according to AllHipHop, Hip-Hop showed up at New York Comic Con in a way nobody saw coming. The two legends sat down with comic artist Sanford Greene to talk about their new X-Men inspired alter egos, part of Legend Has It, the Marvel and Mass Appeal series that also reimagines Ghostface Killah, Raekwon, Mobb Deep, Big L and De La Soul as superheroes.

Greene designed the characters around who these artists already are: Slick Rick's jewelry and regal presence, Nas's gift for turning street stories into cinema. Slick Rick kept the focus bigger than himself, calling Hip-Hop "the future of civilization" that needs protecting and nurturing.

This is what happens when the culture builds its own mythology instead of borrowing someone else's.

At New York Comic Con, the two legends joined artist Sanford Greene to introduce Legend Has It, a comic series built through a partnership between Marvel and Mass Appeal, the media company Nas co-founded.

The series also reimagines Ghostface Killah, Raekwon, Mobb Deep, Big L and De La Soul as superheroes, with every character designed around the artist's real persona rather than a generic template.
